chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The two garments of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in which he entered into Ihram were both Yemeni: Ibri and Zafar, and in them he was shrouded.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.ظَفَارِ: Zafar (a town in Yemen known for its cloth)
key_terms.عِبْرِيٌّ: Ibri (a type of fine cloth from Yemen)

ai.seo_question: What garments did the Prophet wear during Ihram and for his shrouding?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) preference for simple, high-quality Yemeni textiles, specifically the Ibri and Zafar fabrics, which he wore during Ihram and subsequently used for his shroud. In Shia scholarship, this continuity of garment underscores the virtue of modesty and the spiritual significance of the Prophet’s physical remains, linking his state of ritual purity in life to his eternal rest. It serves as a practical model for believers to emulate simplicity in attire while honoring the Sunnah in burial practices.
